messages:
maya: quick sync — starting a lightweight PRD thread for the routing arbitration + degradation ladder work. goal: v1 policy that covers tiers, region affinity, and compatible-model fallbacks. aiming for a canary in 4 weeks.

alex: +1. can we list the high-level customer requirements first? don't want to bake assumptions.

ben: copying Atlas request: 1) regional model preference (eu-west primary), 2) strict data residency — no cross-region fallback unless opt-in, 3) fallback must preserve response shape and streaming behavior.

zoe: also SSoT for billing: if fallback happens, token attribution needs to map to original request owner (so cost/reporting stays accurate).

maya: agreed. initial scope proposal: 
- Tiering: premium / standard / best-effort (controls latency SLO and allowed fallback depth)
- Regions: prefer same-region variants, allowed cross-region only for best-effort or explicit customer opt-in
- Variant compatibility: fallback only to variants declared compatible in compat_map (model family + quantization family + streaming capability)
- Observability: reason codes + trace id + metrics emitted for each arbitration decision

alex: edge cases we should call out up front: incompatible tokenizer, newer architecture (e.g., opt->gpt) not allowed, streaming vs non-streaming mismatch, kv-cache hot/cold invalidations.

zoe: acceptance criteria (candidate):
- A1: requests routed to preferred-region variant >= 99.5% for premium under normal capacity
- A2: fallback to a compatible variant must not change response schema (no sudden JSON->text).
- A3: trace logs include: chosen_variant, reason_code, prior_attempts, region, and cost_bucket.
- A4: customers can opt-out of cross-region fallback via a per-tenant flag.

ben: questions: how do we model "compatibility"? naive name-match is brittle. propose a small manifest per model: {"family":"redwood-1", "quant":"4bit", "streaming":true, "tokenizer":"rwd-v2"}. fallback allowed if family-compatible OR tokenizer-equal + streaming-compat.

maya: that manifest idea is good. we should keep a fallback graph so we can compute transitive safe fallbacks but cap depth to 2 for v1.

alex: policy config example (rough):
```json
{
  "tiers": {
    "premium": {"fallback_depth":0, "cross_region":false},
    "standard": {"fallback_depth":1, "cross_region":true},
    "best_effort": {"fallback_depth":2, "cross_region":true}
  },
  "compat_rules": [
    {"require": ["tokenizer","streaming"], "allow_transitive":false}
  ]
}
```

zoe: can we include a policy reason_code taxonomy? examples: ROUTE_OK, NO_CAPACITY, INCOMPATIBLE_TOKENIZER, CROSS_REGION_FORBIDDEN, FAILSAFE_DEGRADED. product needs those mapped to customer-facing messages.

liz: product note — customers care about determinism. if we do probabilistic routing for load balancing we need clear docs on observability and replayability. also need rollback plan: auto-fallback to previous policy if error rate spikes > 2% in 10m.

maya: rollout plan sketch:
- week 0: spec + compat_map schema + policy config proto
- week 1-2: implement arbitration engine + event/emission hooks (reason_codes)
- week 3: integration tests (compatibility matrix + chaos scenarios)
- week 4: internal canary (small percentage of traffic)
- week 6: customer beta (opt-in tenants)
- post-beta: GA with docs + migration guide

ben: integration test cases to include:
- model variant A (streaming true) -> fallback to B (streaming false) should be rejected
- region primary down -> standard tier should fall back to cross-region when allowed
- cost attribution preserved when fallback occurs
- burst scenario: ensure batching doesn't change route decision semantics

alex: small performance constraint: arbitration should add <1ms p50 per request on the fast path. if we do graph traversal, precompute closures per policy update.

zoe: observability: emit an event per arbitration with fields: {trace_id, tenant_id, tier, chosen_variant, reason_code, fallback_count, latency_added_ms}. these can be tagged for per-tenant dashboards.

deploy-bot: created doc "routing-arbitration-spec" in docs/drive (link: https://notion.fake/routing-arb) by maya.

maya: decisions so far (to be locked after ack):
- compat manifest per model as ben suggested
- fallback depth cap = 2 (configurable per-tier)
- cross-region off by default for premium tenants
- require streaming capability match for any streaming session

alex: ack. i'll prototype the policy proto and a small evaluator next week.

liz: i'll draft the customer-facing FAQ and the opt-in flow.

ben: i'll start the compat_map generator to derive closure and simple compatibility labels.

maya: action items: alex proto + POC (owner alex), ben compat tool (owner ben), zoe metrics/event schema (owner zoe), liz docs + opt-in UX (owner liz). meet friday 10a to review first cut. :calendar: :white_check_mark:

zoe: added test matrix to the shared doc, included a few CSV scenarios for region failover.

alex: quick note — for canary we should include a "simulated incompat" header so we can validate rejection paths end-to-end without taking real model down.

maya: good call. adding that to test plan. thanks all.
